title: Bar Graphs, Dot Plots, Stem-and-Leaf Plots and Scatterplots
seo_title: Grade 5 Data Worksheets: Dot Plots, Stem-and-Leaf Plots and Scatterplots (TEKS 5.9, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.9A represent categorical data with bar graphs or frequency tables and numerical data, including data sets of measurements in fractions or decimals, with dot plots or stem-and-leaf plots; 5.9B represent discrete paired data on a scatterplot; 5.9C solve one- and two-step problems using data from a frequency table, dot plot, bar graph, stem-and-leaf plot, or scatterplot
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 data worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.9A, 5.9B and 5.9C: bar graphs, frequency tables, dot plots with fractions, stem-and-leaf plots with decimals and scatterplots. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Read the scale, the key and the axes before you answer.
key_sub: Scatterplot: x across, y up. Stem-and-leaf: check the key (4 | 7 = 4.7).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Bar graphs and frequency tables show categories, such as favorite foods. Check the scale on a bar graph.
  • Dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots show numbers, including fractions and decimals. Read the key: 4 | 7 can mean 47 or 4.7.
  • A scatterplot shows pairs of numbers as points. Read across for x and up for y.
  • If the points go up from left to right, y tends to increase as x increases.

Examples

Example

Stem-and-leaf plot with key 3 | 4 = 3.4: stems 3, 4; leaves 4 8 | 1 5

Values: 3.4, 3.8, 4.1, 4.5

4.5 − 3.4

Answer: 1.1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong axis on a scatterplotx is across the bottom; y goes up the side.
Misreading the scale on a bar graphFind what each grid line is worth first.
Ignoring the key in a stem-and-leaf plotThe key tells you if 4 | 7 is 47 or 4.7.

Mia filled 15 jars with sand. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the sand in all the jars that hold 1 34 pounds of sand?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 34. Multiply: 2 × 1 34 = 2 × 74 = 144. 144 = 3 12. The total is 3 12 pounds.

items.q: Marcus cut 16 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces that are 1 38 yards long?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 38. Multiply: 2 × 1 38 = 2 × 118 = 228. 228 = 2 34. The total is 2 34 yards.

items.q: Isaac checked 16 cans of leftover paint. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of paint in all the cans that hold 34 gallon of paint?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 34. Multiply: 3 × 34 = 94. 94 = 2 14. The total is 2 14 gallons.

items.q: Grace filled 9 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the trail mix in all the bags that hold 78 pound of trail mix?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 78. Multiply: 2 × 78 = 148. 148 = 1 34. The total is 1 34 pounds.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured 12 beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the beetles that are 38 inch long?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 38. Multiply: 3 × 38 = 98. 98 = 1 18. The total is 1 18 inches.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class poured juice into 14 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of juice in all the glasses that hold 38 cup of juice?
items.e: There are 4 X's above 38. Multiply: 4 × 38 = 128. 128 = 1 12. The total is 1 12 cups.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class poured water into 6 identical beakers. The line plot shows the amounts. Which expression gives the total amount of water in all the beakers?
c: 3 × 14 + 1 × 38 + 2 × 12
2 × 14 + 3 × 38 + 1 × 12
1 × 14 + 3 × 38 + 2 × 12
14 + 38 + 12
items.e: Each value is counted once for every X above it: 2 X's above 14, 3 X's above 38, 1 X above 12. So the total is 2 × 14 + 3 × 38 + 1 × 12.

items.e: Each value is counted once for every X above it: 4 X's above 4 12, 1 X above 4 58, 3 X's above 4 34. So the total is 4 × 4 12 + 1 × 4 58 + 3 × 4 34.

items.q: Sofia weighed 9 rocks. The line plot shows the weights. Which expression gives the total weight of all the rocks?

1 12 + 1 58 + 1 34

items.e: Each value is counted once for every X above it: 2 X's above 1 12, 3 X's above 1 58, 4 X's above 1 34. So the total is 2 × 1 12 + 3 × 1 58 + 4 × 1 34.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured 9 frog jumps. The line plot shows the jump lengths. What is the total length of all the jumps?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 2 × 1 58 = 2 × 138 = 268, 2 × 1 34 = 2 × 74 = 144, 3 × 1 78 = 3 × 158 = 458, 2 × 2 = 4. Add them with denominator 8: 268 + 288 + 458 + 328 = 1318 = 16 38 feet.

items.q: Diego cut 8 pieces of ribbon. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 2 × 34 = 64, 1 × 78 = 78, 2 × 1 = 2, 3 × 1 18 = 3 × 98 = 278. Add them with denominator 8: 128 + 78 + 168 + 278 = 628 = 7 34 yards.

items.q: Isabella measured 9 leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the leaves?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 1 12 = 3 × 32 = 92, 3 × 1 58 = 3 × 138 = 398, 2 × 1 34 = 2 × 74 = 144, 1 × 1 78 = 1 78. Add them with denominator 8: 368 + 398 + 288 + 158 = 1188 = 14 34 inches.

items.q: Jayden recorded the rainfall for 7 days. The line plot shows the rainfall amounts. What is the total rainfall on all the days?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 38 = 98, 1 × 12 = 12, 1 × 58 = 58, 2 × 78 = 148. Add them with denominator 8: 98 + 48 + 58 + 148 = 328 = 4 inches.

items.q: Ximena filled 9 jars with sand. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the sand in all the jars?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 2 × 34 = 64, 2 × 78 = 148, 2 × 1 = 2, 3 × 1 18 = 3 × 98 = 278. Add them with denominator 8: 128 + 148 + 168 + 278 = 698 = 8 58 pounds.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class cut 9 pieces of yarn. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the pieces?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 1 38 = 1 38, 1 × 1 12 = 1 12, 3 × 1 58 = 3 × 138 = 398, 4 × 1 34 = 4 × 74 = 284 = 7. Add them with denominator 8: 118 + 128 + 398 + 568 = 1188 = 14 34 yards.

items.q: Gabriel checked 8 cans of leftover paint. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of paint in all the cans?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 14 = 34, 3 × 38 = 98, 1 × 12 = 12, 1 × 58 = 58. Add them with denominator 8: 68 + 98 + 48 + 58 = 248 = 3 gallons.

items.q: Ethan filled 8 bags of trail mix. The line plot shows the weights. What is the total weight of the trail mix in all the bags?
items.e: Multiply each value by its number of X's: 1 × 12 = 12, 2 × 58 = 108, 2 × 34 = 64, 3 × 78 = 218. Add them with denominator 8: 48 + 108 + 128 + 218 = 478 = 5 78 pounds.

items.q: Mateo measured 16 beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of the beetles that are longer than 34 inch?
items.e: Use only the X's to the right of 34, not the X's above 34. Multiply each value by its number of X's: 3 × 78 = 218, 3 × 1 = 3, 2 × 1 18 = 2 × 98 = 188. Add them with denominator 8: 218 + 248 + 188 = 638 = 7 78 inches.

items.q: Elijah poured juice into 15 glasses. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of juice in the glasses that hold more than 34 cup of juice?
items.e: Use only the X's to the right of 34, not the X's above 34. Multiply each value by its number of X's: 4 × 78 = 288, 5 × 1 = 5. Add them with denominator 8: 288 + 408 = 688 = 8 12 cups.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class poured water into 16 identical beakers. The line plot shows the amounts. What is the total amount of water in the beakers that hold more than 38 liter of water?
items.e: Use only the X's to the right of 38, not the X's above 38. Multiply each value by its number of X's: 2 × 12 = 22 = 1, 3 × 58 = 158, 4 × 34 = 124 = 3. Add them with denominator 8: 88 + 158 + 248 = 478 = 5 78 liters.
